source_text:
Μετανοήσωμεν οὖν ἐξ ὅλης καρδίας, ἵνα μή τις ἡμῶν παραπόληται. εἰ γὰρ ἐντολὰς ἔχομεν ἵνα καὶ τοῦτο πράσσωμεν, ἀπὸ τῶν εἰδώλων ἀποσπᾶν καὶ κατηχεῖν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ψυχὴν ἤδη γινώσκουσαν τὸν θεὸν οὐ δεῖ ἀπόλλυσθαι;
συλλάβωμεν οὖν ἑαυτοῖς καὶ τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας ἀνάγειν περὶ τὸ ἀγαθόν, ὅπως σωθῶμεν ἅπαντες καὶ ἐπιστρέψωμεν ἀλλήλους καὶ νουθετήσωμεν.
καὶ μὴ μόνον ἄρτι δοκῶμεν πιστεύειν καὶ προσέχειν ἐν τῷ νουθετεῖσθαι ἡμᾶς ὑπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὅταν εἰς οἶκον ἀπαλλαγῶμεν, μνημονεύωμεν τῶν τοῦ κυρίου ἐνταλμάτων καὶ μὴ ἀντιπαρελκώμεθα ἀπὸ τῶν κοσμικῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν, ἀλλὰ πυκνότερον προσερχόμενοι πειρώμεθα προκόπτειν ἐν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς τοῦ κυρίον. ἵνα πάντες τὸ αὐτὸ φρονοῦντες συνηγμένοι ὦμεν ἐπὶ τὴν ζωήν:
εἶπεν γὰρ ὁ κύριος: Ἔρχομαι συναγαγεῖν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, φυλὰς καὶ γλώσσας: τοῦτο δὲ λέγει τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς ἐπιφανείας αὐτοῦ, ὅτε ἐλθὼν λυτρώσεται ἡμᾶς, ἕκαστον κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ.
καὶ ὄψονται τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ κράτος οἱ ἄπιστοι, καὶ ξενισθήσονται ἰδόντες τὸ βασίλειον τοῦ κόσμου ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ, λέγοντες: Οὐαὶ ἡμῖν, ὅτι σὺ ἦς, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδειμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐπιστεύομεν καὶ οὐκ ἐπειθόμεθα τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις τοῖς ἀναγγέλλουσιν ἡμῖν περὶ τῆς σωτηρίας ἡμῶν. καὶ ὁ σκώληξ αὐτῶν οὐ τελευτήσει καὶ τὸ πῦρ αὐτῶν οὐ σβεσθήσεται, καὶ ἔσονται εἰς ὅρασιν πάσῃ σαρκί,
τὴν ἡμέραν ἐκείνην λέγει τῆς κρίσεως, ὅταν ὄψονται τοὺς ἐν ἡμῖν ἀσεβήσαντας καὶ παραλογισαμένους τὰς ἐντολὰς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
οἱ δὲ δίκαιοι εὐπραγήσαντες καὶ ὑπομείναντες τὰς βασάνους καὶ μισήσαντες τὰς ἡδυπαθείας τῆς ψυχῆς, ὅταν θεάσωνται τοὺς ἀστοχήσαντας καὶ ἀρνησαμένους διὰ τῶν λόγων ἢ διὰ τῶν ἔργων τὸν Ἰησοῦν, ὅπως κολάζονται δειναῖς βασάνοις πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ, ἔσονται δόξαν διδόντες τῷ θεῷ αὐτῶν λέγοντες, ὅτι ἔσται ἐλπὶς τῷ δεδουλευκότι θεῷ ἐξ ὅλης καρδίας.
thought_title: Repent, gather the weak, and remember the coming judgment
orientation: The preacher is urging the congregation to repent wholeheartedly and to help one another, before quoting the Lord about gathering all nations at his appearing.
pass_a_gloss: Let us repent therefore from the whole heart, so that none of us may be lost. For if we have commandments so that we also do this, to pull away from the idols and to instruct, how much more must a soul that already knows God not be destroyed? Let us help therefore ourselves also to lead up the weak toward the good, so that we all may be saved and may turn one another and may admonish. And let us not only now seem to believe and to pay attention when we are admonished by the elders, but also when we depart to the house, let us remember the commandments of the Lord and let us not be dragged away from the worldly desires, but coming more often let us try to advance in the commandments of the Lord, so that all thinking the same thing we may be gathered together unto the life. For the Lord said: I come to gather all the nations, tribes and tongues. And this he says of the day of his appearing, when having come he will redeem us, each according to his works. And the faithless will see his glory and his might, and they will be astonished seeing the kingdom of the world in Jesus, saying: Woe to us, because you were, and we did not know and we did not believe and we did not obey the elders who announced to us about our salvation. And their worm will not die and their fire will not be quenched, and they will be for a spectacle to all flesh. That day he says of the judgment, when they will see those among us who acted impiously and who falsified the commandments of Jesus Christ. But the righteous, having fared well and having endured the tortures and having hated the pleasures of the soul, when they see those who missed the mark and who denied through words or through deeds Jesus, how they are punished with terrible tortures with unquenchable fire, they will be giving glory to their God saying, that there will be hope for the one who has served God from the whole heart.

lemmas.gloss: be dragged away, be drawn aside

choices.why: The verb means to perish or be destroyed; 'be lost' keeps the passive sense of the middle/passive form and fits the context of souls being destroyed.
The compound verb conveys being pulled aside or dragged away against one's will; 'be dragged away' preserves the passive force and the sense of being diverted from the commandments.
The verb means to deceive or cheat, but with 'commandments' as object it implies treating them falsely or making them void; 'falsified' captures this sense of making the commandments false or void.
The verb literally means to miss the target, and in moral contexts means to fail or err; 'missed the mark' preserves the literal image and the sense of failing to attain the standard.

choices.english: for a spectacle to all flesh
choices.why: The phrase means they will be seen by all flesh, i.e., become a public spectacle; 'for a spectacle to all flesh' keeps the dative of recipient and the sense of being displayed.
rejected: to be seen by all flesh
as a sight to all flesh

bible_refs.note: ὁ σκώληξ αὐτῶν οὐ τελευτήσει καὶ τὸ πῦρ αὐτῶν οὐ σβεσθήσεται
Ἔρχομαι συναγαγεῖν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, φυλὰς καὶ γλώσσας

pass_b_english: So let us repent with our whole heart, so that none of us may be lost. For if we have commandments to do this very thing, to pull people away from idols and instruct them, how much more must a soul that already knows God not be destroyed?
Let us take hold for ourselves, then, and lead the weak up toward the good, so that we may all be saved and may turn one another back and warn one another.

And let us not only seem to believe and pay attention while the elders are warning us. When we have gone home, let us remember the commandments of the Lord and not be dragged away by worldly desires. Instead, let us come together more often and try to make progress in the commandments of the Lord, so that all of us, thinking the same thing, may be gathered together for life.
For the Lord said: "I am coming to gather all the nations, tribes, and languages." This he says about the day of his appearing, when he comes and redeems us, each one according to his works.

And the faithless will see his glory and his power, and they will be astonished when they see the kingdom of the world in Jesus, saying: "Woe to us, because it was you, and we did not know it, and we did not believe, and we did not obey the elders who announced to us about our salvation." And their worm will not die, and their fire will not be quenched, and they will be for a spectacle to all flesh.
This refers to that day of judgment, when they will see those among us who acted impiously and falsified the commandments of Jesus Christ.

But the righteous, who did good and endured torments and hated the pleasures of the soul, when they see those who missed the mark and denied Jesus by words or by deeds being punished with terrible torments in unquenchable fire, will give glory to their God, saying: "There will be hope for the one who has served God with his whole heart."

problems.quote: the kingdom of the world in Jesus
problems.source_quote: τὸ βασίλειον τοῦ κόσμου ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ
problems.why: Brief requires 'kingdom of God' for βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ; here βασίλειον should not be rendered 'kingdom of the world' as though it belongs to the world.
problems.fix: the kingdom of the world in Jesus
problems.ruling: βασίλειον means 'kingdom' but τοῦ κόσμου is genitive 'of the world'; 'kingdom of the world' misrepresents the phrase's likely meaning. The context contrasts worldly vs. divine rule; 'kingdom of God/Christ in Jesus' expected. Source words: τὸ βασίλειον τοῦ κόσμου ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.

The phrase 'the kingdom of the world in Jesus' is a literal rendering of the source and is not a mistranslation; no change is needed.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'flesh' for σάρξ, but here 'soul' is omitted entirely; more critically, ἡδυπαθείας refers to fleshly/sensual pleasures, and 'indulgent pleasures' loses the flesh/spirit contrast central to the homily.
last_rejected.ruling: τῆς ψυχῆς is omitted, but 'indulgent pleasures' adequately renders ἡδυπαθείας; no major meaning change.

last_rejected.why: βασίλειον means 'kingdom' but context demands 'kingly power' or 'royal dominion'; 'kingdom of the world' suggests worldly realm, opposite to intended meaning of Christ's universal sovereignty.
last_rejected.fix: the royal dominion of the world
last_rejected.ruling: βασίλειον can mean kingdom; 'kingdom of the world in Jesus' is a defensible rendering, not a clear error.
